subject: Production impact: Floodlight - request shaping mismatch causing sustained throttling
messages:
From: Sam Wu <sam.wu@floodlight.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: engops@floodlight.ai, procurements@floodlight.ai
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 16:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability alert - sustained 429s and high p99s

Markus / Marissa,

FYI — we started seeing sustained 429s and 2-3s p99s on our inference endpoint at ~09:05 PDT. This is affecting our onboarding cohort (live traffic) and a few payment flows are timing out. We collected a short sample and attached the logs + a traffic spike screenshot.

Key points from our side:
- Traffic pattern spiked by ~3x the hourly baseline between 09:02-09:18.
- Client-side retries are exacerbating the queueing.
- We observe 429s that look like per-tenant rate caps, not global capacity errors.

We need an ETA for mitigation and will escalate internally if we don’t get a workable plan in 30 minutes. Floodlight is due to ship a feature on Monday — this is high severity for them.

—Sam
Sam Wu
Head of Platform
Floodlight AI

Attachments: floodlight_traffic_spike.png (image/png), floodlight-429-sample.log (text/plain)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 16:23:12 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Observability alert - sustained 429s and high p99s

Forwarding Floodlight's report — they included logs and a traffic heatmap. On quick look, the 429s are token-bucket style responses (we can see the bucket refills aligning with a 60s window). The odd part: Floodlight is on Dedicated capacity, but traffic was routed through the hosted fallback for ~4 minutes during the spike. The hosted route has a stricter per-tenant burst cap.

Immediate asks:
- Rishi: can you confirm whether the dedicated pool had burst disabled during the autoscale event?
- Lauren: please surface any config overrides that would cause routing to fall back to hosted for this account.
- Markus: want exec aware — customer is complaining and will escalate if not fixed quickly.

Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Quoted message attached below.

Attachments: tenant-ratecaps.csv (csv)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 16:37:58 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Observability alert - sustained 429s and high p99s

On Thu, May 2, 2028 at 4:23 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Forwarding Floodlight's report — they included logs and a traffic heatmap. On quick look, the 429s are token-bucket style responses (we can see the bucket refills aligning with a 60s window). The odd part: Floodlight is on Dedicated capacity, but traffic was routed through the hosted fallback for ~4 minutes during the spike. The hosted route has a stricter per-tenant burst cap.

I dug in:
- Dedicated pool was healthy and not CPU/GPU-constrained. No PSUs recovered or preemptions in that window.
- Autoscaler briefly marked one node as draining while we applied a patch; the routing policy during drain intentionally shifted new sessions to hosted fallback for state-safety (we have that safeguard).
- Hosted fallback for Floodlight is configured with a per-tenant instantaneous burst of 100 reqs and a refill interval of 60s. Floodlight's normal sustained QPS is 120 but with bursts to 360 during onboarding tests.
- The policy to allow larger bursts on hosted is intentionally conservative for newly onboarded customers; evidently that conservative policy was applied incorrectly during the transient routing.

Root cause (prelim): a conservative hosted-side per-tenant burst cap + a 60s refill window combined with an unexpected routing to hosted during a brief drain. The result: sustained 429s and queueing.

Immediate mitigation I applied (16:34):
1) Raised hosted per-tenant burst cap for Floodlight from 100 -> 1000 for 2 hours.
2) Added a temporary routing override to pin Floodlight back to their Dedicated pool while we finalize a safe autoscaler patch.
3) Opened a tracing runbook so we can see any remaining client retry storms.

Next steps:
- Engineering: push a fix to the autoscaler gating logic to avoid fallback unless the Dedicated pool is unhealthy (not just draining). Target: 24 hrs.
- Account: offer Floodlight an SLA credit and a postmortem with timelines.

I'll prepare a short RCA after we confirm logs.

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, ceo@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 17:02:05 -0700
Subject: Exec summary: Floodlight production impact + proposed customer remediation (urgent)

Team,

Thank you for the quick actions. Send this to execs and legal as an urgent brief (I’m looping CEO). High-level summary we will send to Floodlight in the next 30 minutes — please review and flag edits: 

Summary (for external use):
- What happened: brief autoscaler drain caused requests to be routed to hosted fallback which enforces a conservative per-tenant burst. That cap returned 429s and increased p99 latency for ~16 minutes during our peak.
- Immediate mitigation: raised hosted burst cap and pinned customer back to Dedicated; increased retry-jitter guidance to customer to avoid amplification.
- Impact: onboarding cohort and a small percentage of payment API calls received 429s; Floodlight reported errors that could block their Monday ship.
- Ask: confirm temporary credit and provide concrete remediation timeline (autoscaler gating fix within 24 hours; postmortem within 72 hours).

Action items assigned (internal):
- Rishi: full RCA + rollout to clear autoscaler fallback gating (ETA 24h).
- Marissa: coordinate customer comms + credit paperwork.
- Lauren: audit routing rules for other Dedicated customers to ensure fallback isn't over-restrictive.

Customer-facing note (draft):
Hi Sam — we’re sorry for the impact. We’ve applied a temporary fix (raised burst allowance + pinned traffic) and will follow with a detailed RCA. We will propose an SLA credit and confirm the timeline for the autoscaler patch within 2 hours.

Please reply with any corrections; I’ll send to Floodlight and copy legal.

Markus
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: tenant-ratecaps.csv

From: Sam Wu <sam.wu@floodlight.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: engops@floodlight.ai, procurements@floodlight.ai
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production impact: Floodlight - request shaping mismatch causing sustained throttling

Markus / team,

Thanks for the quick response and the temporary fixes. The traffic looks healthier now and our payment flows have stabilized. A few asks from our side before we close this ticket: 

1) We need the official RCA and the autoscaler fix schedule (we require change-in-production notice at least 48 hrs before the rollout).
2) Please confirm the SLA credit/financial remediation and any implications for our monthly committed capacity.
3) We want to avoid a repeated routed fallback in the future — would Redwood consider a per-account fallback policy that preserves the Dedicated burst profile when the pool is draining but not unhealthy?

We’ll expect the formal RCA and remediation timeline in the next 24 hours.

—Sam
Head of Platform, Floodlight AI
